nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says «هذه هودُ فاعلم» ("this is Hūd, so know") without tanwīn, taking it as the name of the sūra, because if you named a woman Zayd you would not make it fully declinable (diptote). This is the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. ʿĪsā says «هذه هودٌ فاعلم» with tanwīn, taking it as the name of the sūra, and likewise if one named a woman Zayd, because since its middle letter is quiescent it is light, so it is declined fully. If you intend omission, you make it fully declinable according to everyone's view, saying «هذه هودٌ فاعلم», meaning "this is the sūra of Hūd." Sībawayh said: the proof of this is that you say «هذه الرحمن» ("this is al-Raḥmān"); were it not that you mean "the sūra of al-Raḥmān," you would not say «هذه» (feminine "this"). كِتابٌ means "this is a book." أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب». The best that has been said about the meaning of «أحكمت» is: they were all made firm (muḥkama), with no defect in them and no falsehood. And as for ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ آياته: they were made separate so that they may be reflected upon. مِنْ لَدُنْ is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), except that it is indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because it is not fully declinable (ghayr mutamakkina), and what follows it is genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). Sībawayh related «لدن غدوةً يا هذا» ("since morning, O you"), since one says «لد», as Sībawayh recited: [al-Rajaz] 206-
من لد شول فإلى إتلائها
(From the time [the she-camels] had dried up until they were followed by their young.)
The nūn became like the one in «عشرين» ("twenty"), so it put what follows it in the accusative. حَكِيمٍ, i.e. in His actions; خَبِيرٍ, i.e. with the welfare of His creation.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: أَلَّا: al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: it means «بأن لا» ("by [commanding] that not…"); Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is «لئلا» ("so that not…"). تَعْبُدُوا is accusative by «أن».

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ يُمَتِّعْكُمْ مَتاعاً حَسَناً إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنِّي أَخافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذابَ يَوْمٍ كَبِيرٍ (3)
وَأَنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا is conjoined (maʿṭūf); ثُمَّ تُوبُوا is also conjoined. يُمَتِّعْكُمْ is the answer to the command, i.e. He will let you enjoy benefits. مَتاعاً is a noun standing for the maṣdar (verbal noun); حَسَناً is its naʿt (adjective). وَيُؤْتِ is conjoined to «يمتّعكم». كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ are two objects.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
Ibn Jurayj related from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite: (ألا إنهم تثنوني صدورهم ليستخفوا منه). He said: they would not have intercourse with women nor relieve themselves while [their private parts were] exposed [Translator's note: the text reads «وهم يغضون» as written] to the sky, so this verse was revealed. And it is said: some of them would bend over towards others to whisper to them secretly, and their ignorance reached the point that they imagined this would be hidden from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Someone other than Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «إلا إنهم تثنون صدورهم». The meaning of «تثنون» and of the two other readings is close, because it [means] "their breasts fold" until they fold them. Dropping the yāʾ is not permissible except under poetic necessity, as [the poet] said: [al-Mutaqārib] 207-
فهل يمنعني ارتيادي البلاد ... من حذر الموت أن يأتين
(Will my roaming the lands for fear of death keep [death] from coming to me?)
or in a verse-end (ṣila) such as وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَسْرِ [al-Fajr: 4]. يَسْتَغْشُونَ is in the position of the genitive by annexation.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: وَما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is "and there is no creature." إِلَّا عَلَى اللَّهِ رِزْقُها: [«رزقها»] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and according to the Kufans by the adjectival phrase (al-ṣifa) [Translator's note: i.e. by the preceding prepositional phrase].

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَلَئِنْ قُلْتَ إِنَّكُمْ مَبْعُوثُونَ: «إنّ» has kasra because it comes after the verb of saying and begins a new clause; Sībawayh related the fatḥa. لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا with fatḥa on the lām before the nūn, because it is a verb that precedes [its agent] and contains no pronoun; and after it لَيَقُولُنَّ [Translator's note: the text prints لَيَقُولَنَّ; the reference is to the form with ḍamma, e.g. in verse 9/10], because it contains a pronoun.

nahhas-irab:8-9.t: لَيَؤُسٌ is from yaʾisa yayʾasu. Sībawayh related: yaʾisa yayʾisu on the pattern faʿila yafʿilu, and its parallels are ḥasiba yaḥsibu, naʿima yanʿimu and baʾisa yabʾisu. Some of them say: yaʾisa yayʾasu. In the speech of the Arabs only these four verbs among the sound verbs are known to come on the pattern faʿila yafʿilu, and in one of them there is disagreement. So he is yāʾis, and yaʾūs for intensity, and likewise fākhir and fakhūr.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
Yaʿqūb the reader said: and some of the people of Medina read: «إنه لفرُح فخور».
Abū Jaʿfar said: thus, just as you say faṭun, ḥadhar and nadus; and in both dialectal forms quiescence (sukūn) is permissible because of the heaviness of the ḍamma and the kasra.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا is in the position of the accusative. Al-Akhfash said: it is an exception not from the first [category] (disjoined); al-Farrāʾ said: it is an exception from the first [category]. وَلَئِنْ أَذَقْناهُ, i.e. man. He said: because «الإنسان» (man) has the meaning of «الناس» (people).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: فَلَعَلَّكَ تارِكٌ بَعْضَ ما يُوحى إِلَيْكَ وَضائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ: [«ضائق»] is conjoined to «تارك», and «صدرك» is nominative by it. أَنْ يَقُولُوا is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "out of dislike that they should say."

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: قُلْ فَأْتُوا and what follows it. [Translator's note: the entry consists only of these words in the source.]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
فَإِلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ وَأَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ (14)
فَإِلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ: He did not say «لك» ("to you", singular); so it is either a shift in the address, or on the basis that the address to him is like the address to the believers, or on the basis that he is addressed with the address of a group.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
مَنْ كانَ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) by the condition, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is نُوَفِّ إِلَيْهِمْ. The first is past in form and the second is future, as Zuhayr said: [al-Ṭawīl] 208-
ومن هاب أسباب المنايا ينلنه
(And whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him.)
Mujāhid said: We repay him his good deeds in full in this world. Maymūn ibn Mihrān said: there is no one who does a good deed but that its reward is paid in full; if he is a Muslim it is paid in full in this world and the Hereafter, and if he is a disbeliever it is paid in full in this world. And it is said: the meaning is: whoever by his campaign with the Prophet ﷺ sought booty was given it in full and nothing of it was diminished.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَباطِلٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ is its khabar (predicate). Abū Ḥātim said: and the hāʾ [i.e. the object pronoun of «يعملون»] has been omitted. Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not need an omission, because it has the meaning of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "and their work is vain." In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh it is «وباطلا ما كانوا يعملون»; its khabar [Translator's note: so in the text] — «ما» would be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "they used to work vainly."

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: أَفَمَنْ كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "Is one who stands on clear proof from his Lord, and has with him of grace that by which he makes this clear [Translator's note: the text reads «لغيّه», as written], [like another]?" This is according to the view of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan; they both said: وَيَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنْهُ — his tongue. ʿIkrima said, from Ibn ʿAbbās: «ويتلوه شاهد منه» is Gabriel, peace be upon him; on this view it would be "and the clear statement and the proof are followed by a witness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Al-Farrāʾ said: some of them said «ويتلوه شاهد منه» is the Gospel, even though it was before it, i.e. it follows it in confirming [it]. وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى: [«كتاب»] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "and before it the Book of Moses follows it," because the Prophet ﷺ is described in the Book of Moses ﷺ: يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوباً عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْراةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ [al-Aʿrāf: 157]. Abū Ḥātim related from some of them that he read وَمِنْ قَبْلِهِ كِتابَ مُوسى in the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said: the accusative is permissible, being conjoined to the hāʾ, i.e. "and he follows the Book of Moses." إِماماً وَرَحْمَةً are [accusative] as ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
يُضاعَفُ لَهُمُ الْعَذابُ, i.e. in proportion to their disbelief and their sins. ما كانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ: (ما) is in the position of the accusative, on the basis that the meaning is «بما كانوا» ("because they were…"), as you say: «جزيته ما فعل» and «بما فعل» ("I repaid him [for] what he did"). Sībawayh recited: [al-Basīṭ] 209-
أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded.)
It may also be that the meaning is: the punishment is doubled for them forever, and the implied construction in Arabic is "[for] the time of that." It may also be that «ما» is negative, with no position. Al-Farrāʾ said: they could not hear because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, had led them astray in the Preserved Tablet. The fourth answer is from Abū Isḥāq; he said: because of their hatred of the Prophet ﷺ and their enmity towards him, they could not bear to listen to him nor to understand the proofs. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is well known in the speech of the Arabs; it is said, "So-and-so cannot bear to look at so-and-so," when that is burdensome to him. وَما كانُوا يُبْصِرُونَ is conjoined (maʿṭūf).

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ
A mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). One also says «اللذون», and it is not permissible for it to be made indeclinable (mabnī) as the singular is. Concerning its indeclinability there are four views. Al-Akhfash said: «الّذي» was joined to the nūn, so it became like «خمسة عشر» ("fifteen"). It is said: because it is not complete except with a ṣila (relative clause), and a noun is not declined in its middle. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: because it applies to every absent one. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: because it needs what comes after it, like particles, except that it was put in the feminine, dual and plural because it is a naʿt (adjective). Its yāʾ is not given a vowel in the accusative position because it is not declinable [Translator's note: the text reads «بمعرف», as written; «بمعرب» is presumably meant], and for this reason it was dropped in the dual.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: لا جَرَمَ: the scholars have discussed it. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: «جرم» means «حقّ» ("it is true/certain"), and «أنّ» is, according to them both, in the position of the nominative; this is also the view of al-Farrāʾ and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd. Al-Khalīl claimed that «لا» was brought here so that it would be known that the speaker did not begin his speech [from nothing], but was addressing one who had addressed him, and speech is brought to indicate meanings. Abū Isḥāq said: «لا» here is a negation of what they thought would benefit them; the meaning was "that will not benefit them"; جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ, i.e. that action earned them loss; so «أنّ», according to him, is in the position of the accusative. Al-Kisāʾī said: in grammatical analysis [it means] "there is no barring and no preventing from [the fact] that they…". Al-Kisāʾī related four dialectal forms of it: «لا جرم», «ولا عن ذا جرم» and «لا انّ ذا جرم» [Translator's note: only three forms are listed in the text]. He said: and some people of Fazāra say «لا جر أنهم» without the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ related two further forms of it; he said: the Banū ʿĀmir say «لا ذا جرم», and he said: some Arabs say «لا جُرم» with ḍamma on the jīm.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ is the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; آمَنُوا is the ṣila (relative clause); وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَأَخْبَتُوا إِلى رَبِّهِمْ are conjoined to the ṣila. Mujāhid said: «أخبتوا» means "they were at peace (humbly reassured)." Al-Farrāʾ said: «أخبتوا إلى ربهم» and «لربهم» are one [in meaning], and the meaning may be "they directed their humility (ikhbāt) to their Lord." أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is كَالْأَعْمى and what follows it. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. "like the likeness of the blind." Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied construction is: "the likeness of the party of the disbeliever is like the blind and the deaf, and the likeness of the party of the believer is like the hearing and the seeing"; and for this reason هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ ("are they equal?"). Of the conjunctions only the wāw can occur here, because it is for combining; Sībawayh related «مررت بأخيك وصديقك» ("I passed by your brother and your friend").

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ إِنِّي, i.e. "and he said: indeed I…"; and [with] «أني», i.e. «بأنّي» ("[with the message] that I…").

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
فَقالَ الْمَلَأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ: Isḥāq [Translator's note: so in the text; probably Abū Isḥāq] said: «الملأ» are the chiefs, i.e. they are "full" (malīʾūn) of what they say. ما نَراكَ إِلَّا بَشَراً مِثْلَنا: [«بشرا»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and «مثلنا» is annexed to a definite noun yet is indefinite, tanwīn being implied in it, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 210-
يا ربّ مثلك في النّساء غريرة
(Many a guileless one like you among women…)
وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ هُمْ أَراذِلُنا: they are the poor, those without lineage, and those of base crafts; in the ḥadīth [it is said] that they were weavers and cuppers. This was ignorance on their part, because they reproached the Prophet of Allah ﷺ with something in which there is no fault, for the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, are only required to bring proofs and signs, and they are not required to change forms and appearances. They are sent to all people, so when those [of low standing] among them embraced Islam, no deficiency attached to them from that, because they are required to accept the Islam of everyone of them who embraces Islam. بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ: [from] badā yabdū, when something appears, as [the poet] said: [al-Kāmil] 211-
فاليوم حين بدون للنّظّار
(So today, when they appeared to the onlookers…)
It may be that «بادي الرأي» is from badaʾa ("to begin") with the hamza lightened; Abū ʿAmr pronounced the hamza fully and read بادِئَ الرَّأْيِ [Translator's note: the text prints بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ here; the hamzated form is what is described]. Abū Isḥāq said: its accusative is with the meaning «في بادئ الرأي» ("at first thought"). Abū Jaʿfar said: the grammarians have not explained its accusative, as far as I know, beyond this; so it may be that «في» was omitted, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَاخْتارَ مُوسى قَوْمَهُ [al-Aʿrāf: 155], and it may be that the meaning is "an apparent following."

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related أَنُلْزِمْكُمُوها with the first mīm quiescent, for lightening [Translator's note: the text prints the ordinary vowelled form]. Sībawayh permitted the like of this and recited: [al-Sarīʿ] 212-
فاليوم أشرب غير مستحقب ... إثما من الله ولا واغل
(So today I drink, not incurring a sin from Allah, nor intruding [uninvited].)
And according to the view of Yūnus, outside the Qurʾān, «أنلزمكمها» is permissible, treating the pronoun like an overt noun, as you say «أنلزمكم تلك» ("shall we force that upon you?").

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ: the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl, and it may be dropped, so you say «تذكّرون» [Translator's note: the text does not distinguish the two forms in writing; the form with a single, unassimilated tāʾ, tadhakarūna, is presumably meant].

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: وَلا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِنْدِي خَزائِنُ اللَّهِ: he declared his humility and his lowliness before Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and that he does not claim what is not his of the treasuries of Allah, Majestic and Mighty — which are His favours upon whomever He wills of His servants — and that he does not know the Unseen, because no one knows the Unseen but Allah, Majestic and Mighty. وَلا أَقُولُ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ, i.e. nor do I say that my rank with Allah, Majestic and Mighty, is the rank of the angels. The scholars have said: the benefit of this statement is to indicate that the angels are superior to the prophets, Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, because of their constancy in obedience and the continuity of their worship until the Day of Resurrection. وَلا أَقُولُ for you, nor لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِي أَعْيُنُكُمْ: the original is «تزدريهم»; the hāʾ and mīm were omitted because of the length of the noun [i.e. the relative clause]. The dāl is substituted for a tāʾ, because the zāy is voiced and the tāʾ is unvoiced, so a voiced letter from its place of articulation was substituted for the tāʾ. إِنِّي إِذاً لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ, i.e. if I said this; and «إذن» is inoperative (mulghā) because it is in the middle.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: And from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَأَكْثَرْتَ جِدالَنا. In the speech of the Arabs, al-jadal is going to excess in dispute and debate; it is derived from al-jadl, which is tight twisting. The falcon is called ajdal because of its strength among birds.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: وَلا يَنْفَعُكُمْ نُصْحِي إِنْ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَنْصَحَ لَكُمْ, i.e. because you do not accept advice.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: إِجْرامِي is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ajrama, and «أَجرامي» is the plural of jurm; one says both ajrama and jarama.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَأُوحِيَ إِلى نُوحٍ: concerning the full declension of «نوح» there are two views. One is that it is non-Arabic but light, because it consists of three letters; the other is that it is Arabic. ʿIkrima said: he was named Nūḥ only because he used to lament (niyāḥa) much over himself. He said: he boarded the ship when ten [nights] of Rajab had passed, وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ [Hūd: 44] when ten [nights] of Muḥarram had passed; that is six months. Its length was three hundred cubits, and its width and height thirty cubits. أَنَّهُ is in the position of the nominative as the noun of a verb whose agent is not named (deputy agent, nāʾib fāʿil), and it may be in the position of the accusative, the implied construction being «بأنه». لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِنْ قَوْمِكَ إِلَّا مَنْ قَدْ آمَنَ: [«من»] is in the position of the nominative by «يؤمن». فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ, i.e. do not grieve to the point of being miserable (bāʾis).

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنا: it is said its meaning is "under Our protection"; it is said "with Our knowledge"; and it is said: because the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, were directing that. وَلا تُخاطِبْنِي فِي الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا, i.e. do not ask Me concerning them, for I am going to drown them.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: وَكُلَّما is an adverb (ẓarf). مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُ: al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī said: one says «سخرت به» and «منه» ("I mocked him").

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ: al-Kisāʾī said: some people of the Ḥijāz say «سو تعلمون». He said: and whoever says «ستعلمون» has dropped both the wāw and the fāʾ. The Kufans related «سف تعلمون». The Basrans know only «سوف يفعل» and «سيفعل», [as] two forms, neither of which is derived from the other.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيها مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ: [«اثنين»] is in the position of the accusative by «احمل». وَأَهْلَكَ is conjoined to it. إِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ: «من» is in the position of the accusative by the exception. وَمَنْ آمَنَ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to «اثنين», or if you wish to «أهلك». وَما آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ: [«قليل»] is nominative by «آمن», and it is not permissible to make it accusative as an exception, because the speech before it is not complete. But the benefit of the entry of «إلّا» and «ما» is that if you said «آمن معه فلان وفلان» ("so-and-so and so-and-so believed with him"), it would be possible that others besides them had also believed; but when you bring «ما» and «إلّا», you affirm [belief] for what comes after إنّ [Translator's note: so in the text; «إلّا» is presumably meant] and negate it of others.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: وَقالَ ارْكَبُوا فِيها بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْراها وَمُرْساها with ḍamma on both mīms is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Basra, except for those of them who deviated. Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْراها with fatḥa on the mīm and وَمُرْساها with ḍamma on the mīm [Translator's note: the text prints the first word as مُجْراها/مَجْراها without distinguishing; the description is translated as written]. It is reported from Yaḥyā ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Aʿmash, from Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb: «باسم الله مَجراها ومَرساها» with fatḥa on the mīm in both. Mujāhid, Muslim ibn Jundub and ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «باسم الله مجريها ومرسيها». The first reading has the meaning "in the name of Allah [be] its running and its anchoring (ijrāʾuhā wa-irsāʾuhā)", nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). It may be in the position of the accusative, the implied construction being "in the name of Allah, at the time of its running," as you say «أنا أجيئك مقدم الحاجّ» ("I will come to you at the arrival of the pilgrims"). It is said: the implied construction is "in the name of Allah [is] the place of its running," then «موضع» ("place") was omitted and «مجراها» put in its place. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: when he said "In the name of Allah," it ran, and when he said "In the name of Allah," it anchored; and the bāʾ is attached to «اركبوا». «مَجراها» with fatḥa on the mīm is from jarat majran ("it ran"), and «مَرساها» with fatḥa on the mīm is from rasat rusuwwan wa-marsan ("it anchored"), when it stood firm. «مجريها» is a naʿt (adjective) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in the position of the genitive; it may be in the position of the nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the one who makes it run and makes it anchor"; and the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible, with the meaning «أعني» ("I mean").

nahhas-irab:42-42.t:
وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ: according to the view of Sībawayh, وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ with a slurred [vowel] (mukhtalas) وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ is permissible. Sībawayh recited: [al-Wāfir] 213-
له زجل كأنه صوت حاد
(It has a din as though it were the voice of a camel-driver singing.)
As for وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وَكانَ [Translator's note: the text does not mark the vowel of this variant; from what follows it is «ابنهَ», with fatḥa on the hāʾ], it is an anomalous (shādhdh) reading. Abū Ḥātim claimed that it is permissible on the basis that he means «ابنها» ("her son") and then the alif is dropped, as you say «ابنه» and drop the wāw. Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū Ḥātim said is not permissible according to the doctrine of Sībawayh, because the alif is light, so its dropping is not permissible, whereas the wāw is heavy and may be dropped. وَكانَ فِي مَعْزِلٍ: «معزل» is the noun of place and the maṣdar (verbal noun). يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا; and ʿĀṣim read يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا with fatḥa on the yāʾ. Abū Isḥāq said: in Arabic «يا بنيّ اركب معنا» is permissible [Translator's note: the vowelling distinguishing this variant is not shown in the text; from the comparison, «يا بُنَيِّيَ», with an overt yāʾ, is presumably meant], as you say «يا غلامي أقبل» ("O my servant, come"), and likewise يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ [al-Zumar: 53]; and «يا بني اركب معنا», on the basis that you drop the yāʾ and leave the kasra indicating it, as you say «يا غلامِ أقبل». As for the reading of ʿĀṣim, it is problematic. Abū Ḥātim said: he means «يا بنيّاه» and then [the ending] was dropped. Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān holding that this is not permissible, because the alif is light and is not dropped.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I know of none of the grammarians who allowed discussion in this except Abū Isḥāq, for he claimed that the fatḥa is from two angles and the kasra from two angles. The fatḥa is on the basis that alif is substituted for the yāʾ, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said, at times, يا وَيْلَتى [Hūd: 72] [Translator's note: the text prints يا وَيْلَنا], and as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 214-
فيا عجبا من رحلها المتحمّل
(O how amazing, [the burden of] her saddle being carried!)
so he means «يا بنيّا», then the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as you say «جاءني عبدا الله» in the dual [Translator's note: the text prints «عبد الله»; the dual is what is described]. The other angle is that the alif is dropped because the vocative is a place of omission; but [as for the kasra, it is] on the basis that the yāʾ is dropped, and the other angle is on the basis that he drops it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. وَلا تَكُنْ مَعَ الْكافِرِينَ: this indicates — and Allah knows best — that Noah ﷺ did not know that he was a disbeliever, and that he thought he was a believer [Translator's note: the text reads «أنا مؤمن», as written].

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: قالَ لا عاصِمَ الْيَوْمَ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ: on the basis of absolute negation (tabriʾa; the lā of generic negation). «لا عاصمٌ اليومَ» is permissible, «لا» having the meaning of «ليس» [Translator's note: the text does not show the tanwīn distinguishing this variant]. إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ is in the position of the accusative as an exception not from the first [category] (disjoined), and it may be in the position of the nominative on the basis that «عاصم» has the meaning of «معصوم» ("protected"), like ماءٍ دافِقٍ [al-Ṭāriq: 6]. Among the best that has been said about it is that «من» is in the position of the nominative and the meaning is "none protects today from the command of Allah except the Merciful One," i.e. except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. This is good because you have not made «عاصم» mean «معصوم» and so taken it out of its proper category.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: وَقِيلَ يا أَرْضُ ابْلَعِي ماءَكِ: it is said that this is figurative (majāz), because it is inanimate; and it is said that something was placed in it by which it could discern. The one who said that it is figurative said: if the speech of the Arabs and the non-Arabs were searched, nothing like this verse would be found in it, in the beauty of its arrangement, the eloquence of its description and the meanings it comprises. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related «بلِعت» and «بلَعت» [Translator's note: the two vowellings are not shown in the text; balaʿtu and baliʿtu are presumably meant]. وَغِيضَ الْماءُ: one says «غاض الماء» ("the water subsided") and «غضته» ("I made it subside"), and «غُيض الماء» with ḍamma on the ghayn is permissible. وَاسْتَوَتْ عَلَى الْجُودِيِّ: the declension is shown in it because the yāʾ is doubled and what precedes it is quiescent. Al-Farrāʾ related «واستوت على الجوديْ» with the yāʾ quiescent, because what precedes it has kasra and it is light (undoubled). وَقِيلَ بُعْداً لِلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ: the ones who said this, according to what is reported, were Noah ﷺ and the believers, i.e. "may Allah remove the wrongdoers far away," so they were removed far (buʿdan), as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: إِنَّ ابْنِي: the noun (ism) of «إنّ»; مِنْ أَهْلِي is in the position of the khabar (predicate). وَإِنَّ وَعْدَكَ الْحَقُّ: the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar. وَأَنْتَ أَحْكَمُ الْحاكِمِينَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ: we have already mentioned it. فَلا تَسْئَلْنِ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ, i.e. [do not ask] me about one whom you do not know to be a believer. إِنِّي أَعِظُكَ, i.e. I admonish you with My prohibition and My restraint, so that you will not be [one of the ignorant]; and the Basrans take the implied construction to be "out of dislike that you should be."

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: I.e. I ask You to grant me success and be gracious to me so that I do not ask that. وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي indicates that the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, commit sins. أَكُنْ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ, i.e. [losers of] Your mercy on the Day of Resurrection.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: قِيلَ يا نُوحُ اهْبِطْ, i.e. from the ship, بِسَلامٍ, i.e. in safety. وَبَرَكاتٍ عَلَيْكَ, i.e. abiding blessings; [barakāt] is derived from the kneeling (burūk) of a camel, which is its staying firm and remaining in place. مِمَّنْ مَعَكَ: «من» is partitive, and it may be for clarifying the genus. وَأُمَمٌ سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ, i.e. and there will be nations. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: as you say, «كلّمت زيدا وعمرو جالس» ("I spoke to Zayd while ʿAmr was sitting"). Al-Farrāʾ permitted, outside the [canonical] reading, «وأمما», its implied construction being "and We will give enjoyment to nations."

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ, i.e. those reports; and in another place «ذلك», i.e. that report. فَاصْبِرْ, i.e. be patient with the harm of your people as these messengers, Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, were patient.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: وَإِلى عادٍ أَخاهُمْ هُوداً: [«أخاهم»] is accusative with the meaning "and We sent." Abū Isḥāq said: he was called their brother because he was from among them, or because he was of the children of Adam, peace be upon him, as they were of the children of Adam. ما لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلهٍ غَيْرُهُ [in the genitive] according to the wording, «غيرُه» [nominative] according to the position, and «غيرَه» [accusative] according to the exception. إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلَّا مُفْتَرُونَ, i.e. in taking a god other than Him you are nothing but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: يا قَوْمِ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً: the yāʾ was dropped because the vocative is a place of omission due to its frequency; keeping it is permissible because it is a noun.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ is jussive because it is an answer and contains the meaning of requital (mujāzāt). مِدْراراً is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it contains the meaning of intensity; the Arabs drop the hāʾ [of the feminine] in mifʿāl on the basis of attribution (nasab). وَيَزِدْكُمْ is conjoined to «يرسل».

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: إِنْ نَقُولُ إِلَّا اعْتَراكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنا: on the basis of the masculine of «بعض»; the feminine is permissible according to the meaning.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ, i.e. I am content with His judgement and trust in His help. وما مِنْ دَابَّةٍ is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِناصِيَتِها, i.e. He directs it however He wills and holds it back from whatever He wills, i.e. so they cannot reach [to do] me harm. Everything that has a soul is called dābb and dābba, the hāʾ being for intensity (mubālagha). إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ: it is said that its meaning is that there is no defect in His management and no disparity in His creation.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا is in the position of the jussive, and for that reason the nūn was dropped from it. The original is «تتولّوا»; one tāʾ was dropped because of the combination of two tāʾs, and because the meaning is known [Translator's note: the text reads «وإنّ المعنى معروف», as written]. فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إِلَيْكُمْ has the meaning "I have made clear to you." وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْماً غَيْرَكُمْ is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), and it may be conjoined to what is required after the fāʾ. The jussive is permissible outside the Qurʾān, like وَنَذَرُهُمْ فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ [al-Anʿām: 110], and likewise وَلا تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئاً.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: وَلَمَّا جاءَ أَمْرُنا نَجَّيْنا هُوداً وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا: because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah the Exalted, even if he has righteous deeds; and something like this is [reported] from the Prophet ﷺ. It is said: the meaning of بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَّا is "by Our having made clear to them the guidance, which is a mercy."

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: وَتِلْكَ عادٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ related that among the Arabs are some who do not decline «عاد» fully (treating it as a diptote), i.e. they make it a name of the tribe.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: أَلا إِنَّ عاداً كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. they were ungrateful for the favour of their Lord. He said: one says «كفرته» and «كفرت به», and «شكرت له» and «شكرته».

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
وَإِلى ثَمُودَ أَخاهُمْ صالِحاً: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read «وإلى ثمودٍ أخاهم صالحا» [Translator's note: the tanwīn of this variant is not shown in the text], and they both declined «ثمود» fully throughout the Qurʾān. Ḥamza did not decline «ثمود» fully anywhere in the Qurʾān, and the same is reported from al-Ḥasan. The rest of the readers differed about it: they declined it fully in one place and not in another. Abū ʿUbayd claimed that were it not for contradicting the written text (al-sawād), the right course would be not to decline it fully, since the feminine predominates in it. Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū ʿUbayd, may Allah have mercy on him, said — that the feminine predominates in it — is a rejected statement, because «ثمود» is called a ḥayy (clan, masculine) and is called a qabīla (tribe, feminine), and "tribe" does not predominate in it; rather, according to Sībawayh, the matter is the opposite of what he said. The better course according to Sībawayh, for [names] of which "Banū so-and-so" is not said, is full declension, such as Quraysh, Thaqīf and the like, and likewise «ثمود». The reason for this is that since the masculine is the original, and it can be treated as masculine and feminine, the original and the lighter is preferable; yet the feminine is good and fully acceptable. Sībawayh recited for the feminine: [al-Kāmil] 215-
غلب المساميح الوليد سماحة ... وكفى قريش المعضلات وسادها
(Al-Walīd surpassed the generous in generosity, spared Quraysh their hardships and became their chief.)
غَيْرُهُ هُوَ أَنْشَأَكُمْ: assimilating the hāʾ into the hāʾ is not permissible except in the dialect of those who drop the wāw in connected speech. إِنَّ رَبِّي قَرِيبٌ مُجِيبٌ, i.e. near in answering.

nahhas-irab:64-64.t: هذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is said: "the she-camel of Allah" because He brought it out for them from a mountain as they had requested, on condition that they would believe. لَكُمْ آيَةً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَذَرُوها is a command, and for that reason the nūn was dropped from it. One does not say «وذر» or «واذر» except anomalously; the grammarians have two views about it. Sībawayh said: they made do with «ترك» instead of it. Someone else said: since the wāw is heavy and there is in the language a verb with its meaning that has no wāw, they abandoned it. تَأْكُلْ فِي أَرْضِ اللَّهِ is jussive because it is the answer to the command. Abū Isḥāq said: it may be nominative as a ḥāl and as resumptive. وَلا تَمَسُّوها is jussive by the prohibition. Al-Farrāʾ said: بِسُوءٍ, i.e. by hamstringing [her]. فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ is the answer to the prohibition. عَذابٌ قَرِيبٌ, [i.e. near] from her hamstringing.

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: فَعَقَرُوها فَقالَ تَمَتَّعُوا, i.e. with the favours of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, before the punishment. ثَلاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān).

nahhas-irab:66-66.t:
Abū Ḥātim said: Abū Zayd told us from Abū ʿAmr that he read وَمِنْ خِزْيِ يَوْمِئِذٍ, assimilating the yāʾ into the yāʾ, with annexation and kasra on the mīm of «يومئذ». Abū Jaʿfar said: what the grammarians such as Sībawayh and those close to him relate from Abū ʿAmr in the like of this is concealment (ikhfāʾ); as for assimilation, it is not permissible because two quiescent letters would meet, and kasra on the zāy is not permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever reads «من خزيِ يومِئذ» drops the tanwīn and annexes; whoever uses tanwīn puts «يومئذ» in the accusative as an adverb; and whoever drops the tanwīn and uses the accusative, saying «ومن خزيِ يومَئذ», has two implied analyses according to the grammarians. Sībawayh's analysis is that it is indeclinable (mabnī), because an adverb of time is not fully established in declension, so when it was annexed to something indeclinable it was made indeclinable; and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 216-
على حين ألهى الناس جلّ أمورهم
(At a time when most of their affairs distracted people…)
Abū Ḥātim said: he treated «يوم» and «إذ» like «خمسة عشر» ("fifteen").

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: وَأَخَذَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ: they were shouted at and died. [The verb] is masculine because «الصيحة» and «الصياح» ("the shout") are one. فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دِيارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ: it is said: fallen on their faces.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا إِبْراهِيمَ بِالْبُشْرى: it is said: [the good news] of a son; and it is said: they gave him the good news that they were messengers of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and that he had nothing to fear. قالُوا سَلاماً: there are two analyses of its accusative. It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun); the other analysis is that it is accusative by «قالوا», as one says «قالوا خيرا» ("they said good"). The exegesis on this [second] view: Yaḥyā al-Qaṭṭān related from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: قالُوا سَلاماً, i.e. [they said] something sound (sadad). قالَ سَلامٌ: there are two analyses of its nominative. One is with an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is peace" and "my affair is peace"; the other has the meaning "peace be upon you." Al-Farrāʾ said: if both were accusative or both nominative, it would be permissible. However al-Farrāʾ gave a reason why the first is accusative and the second nominative, saying: they said "peace (salāman)," and Abraham ﷺ said, "it is peace, if Allah wills." فَما لَبِثَ أَنْ جاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ: Sībawayh holds that «أن» is in the position of the accusative; he said: you say «لا يلبث أن يأتيك», i.e. "[he will not delay] from coming to you." Al-Farrāʾ permitted its position to be [nominative] by «لبث», i.e. "his coming was not slow."

nahhas-irab:70-70.t:
فَلَمَّا رَأى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لا تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ: this is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; the dialect of Asad and Tamīm is «أنكرهم». Imruʾ al-Qays said: [al-Ṭawīl] 217-
لقد أنكرتني بعلبك وأهلها
(Baalbek and its people have found me strange.)
And it is related for al-Aʿshā: [al-Basīṭ] 218-
وأنكرتني وما كان الّذي نكرت ... من الحوادث إلّا الشّيب والصّلعا
(She found me strange, and what she found strange among the happenings was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)
وَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً: Sībawayh said: some people of Rabīʿa say «منهِم», making it follow the kasra, the quiescent letter not being for them a strong barrier. Abū Jaʿfar said: it is said that he felt fear of them only because he used to live apart in a remote place, so he feared that they had resolved upon some evil against him; and when guests did not eat, it was only because they intended evil.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t:
وَامْرَأَتُهُ قائِمَةٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). فَضَحِكَتْ: we have already mentioned it. It is said: she laughed only because they brought the calf back to life by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and when it rejoined its mother she laughed, and when she laughed they gave her the good news of Isaac. وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ: its nominative is from two angles. One is as a mubtadaʾ, being in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. they gave her the good news of Isaac, with Jacob facing him [i.e. coming after him]. The other analysis is that the implied construction is "and after Isaac, Jacob will come into being," and on this [view] it is not included in the good news. Ḥamza and ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read وَمِنْ وَراءِ إِسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ [Translator's note: here the accusative/genitive-form «يعقوبَ» is meant; the text does not distinguish it from the nominative variant above]. Al-Kisāʾī, al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim take «يعقوب» to be in the position of the genitive; according to the doctrine of Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, it is in the position of the accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: the genitive is not permissible except by repeating the genitive-governing word.
Sībawayh said: if you said «مررت بزيد أوّلَ من أمس وأمسِ عمرو» ("I passed by Zayd the day before yesterday, and yesterday ʿAmr"), it would be ugly and vile, because you have separated the genitive noun from what shares with it, which is the wāw, just as you would separate the preposition from its genitive. Abū Jaʿfar said: the implied construction would be "and after Isaac We granted him Jacob," as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 219-
جئني بمثل بني بدر لقومهم ... أو مثل أسرة منظور بن سيّار
أو عامر بن طفيل في مركّبه ... أو حادثا يوم نادى القوم يا حار
(Bring me the like of Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār, or ʿĀmir ibn Ṭufayl in his lineage, or Ḥārith on the day the people called out "O Ḥār!")

nahhas-irab:72-72.t: قالَتْ يا وَيْلَتى, with the alif pronounced with imāla (inclination towards i) and with full (tafkhīm) pronunciation. Abū Isḥāq said: its origin is the yāʾ, and alif was substituted for the yāʾ. وَهذا بَعْلِي: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). شَيْخاً is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Isḥāq said: the accusative of the ḥāl here is among the subtle and obscure points of grammar, because if you say «هذا زيد قائما» ("this is Zayd, standing") and the person addressed does not know Zayd, it is not permissible, because he would not be Zayd only as long as he is standing, so that when that ceased he would not be Zayd; but if he knows Zayd, the sentence is sound. The governing factor (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl is the [sense of] drawing attention and pointing. Al-Akhfash said: in the reading of Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd it is «وهذا بعلي شيخ». Al-Farrāʾ said: in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd it is «وهذا بعلي شيخ». Abū Jaʿfar said: the nominative is from five angles. You say «هذا زيد قائم»: «زيد» is a badal (substitute) for «هذا» and «قائم» is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. «هذا» may be a mubtadaʾ with «زيد» and «قائم» two khabars; Sībawayh related «هذا حلو حامض» ("this is sweet-sour"). «قائم» may be nominative with an implied «هذا» or «هو». It may be nominative as a badal of «زيد». The fifth analysis is that «هذا» is a mubtadaʾ, «زيد» explains it [i.e. ʿaṭf bayān, explicative apposition], and «قائم» is the khabar.

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكاتُهُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is in عَلَيْكُمْ. Sībawayh related «عليكِم» with kasra on the kāf because of its proximity to the yāʾ. أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ is accusative as a vocative, and Sībawayh calls it specification (takhṣīṣ). إِنَّهُ حَمِيدٌ, i.e. praised; مَجِيدٌ, i.e. glorious.

nahhas-irab:74-75.t: فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْراهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ وَجاءَتْهُ الْبُشْرى يُجادِلُنا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ: the doctrine of al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī is that «يجادلنا» stands in place of «جادلنا» ("he argued with Us"). Abū Jaʿfar said: since the answer of «لمّا» must be in the past, the imperfect was put in its place, just as the condition must be in the imperfect and the past was put in its place. In another answer, «يجادلنا» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he set about arguing with Us," and this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. One says «أناب» when one returns; so Abraham ﷺ was returning to Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in all his affairs.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: وَلَمَّا جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا لُوطاً سِيءَ بِهِمْ: if you wish, you may give the sīn ḍamma, because its origin is ḍamma. The original is «سُوِئَ بهم», from al-sūʾ (evil); the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the sīn, and it turned into yāʾ. If you lighten the hamza, you cast its vowel onto the yāʾ and say «سِيَ بهم», lightened. Doubling [the yāʾ] is an anomalous dialect. وَضاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً is [accusative] as clarification (tamyīz). وَقالَ هذا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ, and «عصبصب» for intensity, i.e. hateful, with evil gathered in it. «قد عصب» means "it was bound up with evil like a band (ʿiṣāba)"; and from them comes the saying «عصابة» and «عصبة» (a band), i.e. united in word and gathered in themselves; a man's ʿaṣaba are those united with him in lineage; «تعصّبت لفلان» means "I became like his ʿaṣaba" [Translator's note: the text reads «كعضبته», as written]; and a maʿṣūb man is one compactly built.

nahhas-irab:78-78.t: وَجاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إِلَيْهِ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). قالَ يا قَوْمِ هؤُلاءِ بَناتِي: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). هُنَّ أَطْهَرُ لَكُمْ: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read هُنَّ أَطْهَرَ لَكُمْ [Translator's note: the text prints أَطْهَرُ throughout this entry; the accusative variant is what is discussed]. Sībawayh related: "Ibn Marwān wrapped himself up in solecism (iḥtabā fī al-laḥn)," i.e. when he read هُنَّ أَطْهَرَ لَكُمْ. Abū Ḥātim said: Ibn Marwān was the reader of the people of Medina. Al-Kisāʾī said: هُنَّ أَطْهَرَ لَكُمْ is correct, making «هنّ» a support (ʿimād, i.e. the separating pronoun). Abū Jaʿfar said: the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Akhfash is that this is not permissible and that «هنّ» cannot be a ʿimād here. He said: it is a ʿimād only where the sentence is not complete except with what comes after it, such as «كان زيد هو أخاك» ("Zayd was your brother"), to indicate by it that «الأخ» is not a naʿt (adjective). Abū Isḥāq said: and it indicates that «كان» needs a khabar. Someone else said: it indicates that the khabar is definite or close to it. وَلا تُخْزُونِ in my guests, i.e. do not humiliate me nor abase me. «ضيف» (guest) applies to two and to many in the form of the singular, because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); dual and plural are also permissible for it. أَلَيْسَ مِنْكُمْ رَجُلٌ رَشِيدٌ, i.e. one who would guide you and forbid you.

nahhas-irab:79-79.t: قالُوا لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما لَنا فِي بَناتِكَ مِنْ حَقٍّ, i.e. because we have not married them.

nahhas-irab:81-81.t:
قالُوا يا لُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَنْ يَصِلُوا إِلَيْكَ, i.e. they will not reach you with anything harmful. It is related that when they said this to him, he left the way open between his people and entering, and Gabriel ﷺ passed his hand over their eyes and they were blinded, and over their hands and they withered, so they returned to their dwellings in haste. فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ: one says «سرى» and «أسرى» when one travels by night; they are two eloquent dialectal forms. وَلا يَلْتَفِتْ مِنْكُمْ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ is accusative by the exception, and this is the clear reading.
The meaning is "so travel with your family except your wife," and He, Majestic and Mighty, has said كانَتْ مِنَ الْغابِرِينَ, i.e. among those who remained behind; he did not take her out — though something other than this has been said about it. What also indicates the accusative is that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «فأسر بأهلك إلا امرأتك». It has been said that the meaning is "let none of you turn to what he has left behind, and let him go out with Lot ﷺ." Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read إلا امرأتُك in the nominative, as a badal (substitute). A group, among them Abū ʿUbayd, rejected this reading. Abū ʿUbayd said: if it were so, then «ولا يلتفتُ» would be in the nominative. Someone else said: how could he command her to turn round? Abū Jaʿfar said: this imputation by Abū ʿUbayd and others against someone like Abū ʿAmr, with his eminence and his standing in Arabic, ought not to be. The interpretation for it is according to what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd related; he said: this is as a man says to his doorkeeper, «لا يخرج فلان» ("let so-and-so not go out"): the wording of the prohibition is to so-and-so, but its meaning is to the one addressed, i.e. "do not let him go out." So likewise "let none of you turn round except your wife." Similar is «لا يقم أحد إلّا زيد» ("let no one stand except Zayd"): its meaning is "forbid them from standing, except Zayd"; and another analysis is that its meaning is "command Zayd alone to stand."
أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ: because Lot ﷺ urged them to hasten the punishment out of his anger at his people. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read أَلَيْسَ الصُّبُحُ with ḍamma on the bāʾ, and it is a dialectal form.

nahhas-irab:82-82.t: جَعَلْنا عالِيَها سافِلَها: two objects. Abū ʿUbayd related from al-Farrāʾ that millstones are sometimes called سِجِّيلٍ; and Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm related from him that sijjil is clay that is baked until it becomes like millstones. مَنْضُودٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of «سجيل».

nahhas-irab:83-83.t: مُسَوَّمَةً is a naʿt (adjective) of «حجارة». Al-Farrāʾ said: they claimed that they were streaked with red and black on white, and that is their marking (taswīm), i.e. their marks. He said: وَما هِيَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ, meaning the people of Lot, بِبَعِيدٍ; he said: they would not miss them.

nahhas-irab:84-84.t: وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ أَخاهُمْ شُعَيْباً: «مدين» is a diptote because it is the name of a town.

nahhas-irab:86-86.t: بَقِيَّتُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). We have already mentioned its meaning, and it has been said that the meaning is: what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, leaves for you of His provision and His protection خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ than what you take by short-measuring and injustice. وَما أَنَا عَلَيْكُمْ بِحَفِيظٍ, i.e. it is not possible for me to protect you from the removal of the favours of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, from you because of your sins.

nahhas-irab:87-87.t: قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا: «أن» is in the position of the accusative; al-Kisāʾī said: its position is genitive with an implied bāʾ. أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ فِي أَمْوالِنا ما نَشؤُا: (أن) is in the position of the accusative and nothing else, conjoined to (ما); the meaning is "or [does it command you] that we abandon doing with our wealth what we will." Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the implied construction is "or does it forbid us to do with our wealth what we will." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Qays read «أو أن تفعل في أموالنا ما تشاء» with tāʾ, so «أن» in this reading is conjoined to the first «أن». إِنَّكَ لَأَنْتَ الْحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned it, and there is an addition in it that is better than what preceded, and because what precedes it indicates its soundness, i.e. "you are the forbearing, the right-minded, so how do you command us to abandon what our fathers worship?" What indicates it is أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا: when they saw how much he prayed and worshipped, and that he was forbearing and right-minded, they rejected [the idea] that he would command you [Translator's note: so in the text; "them" is presumably meant] to abandon what their fathers used to worship. This is severe ignorance or obstinacy, and what comes after it also indicates it.

nahhas-irab:88-88.t: I.e. "should I not, then, forbid you from going astray?" وَما أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخالِفَكُمْ: [«أن أخالفكم»] is in the position of the accusative by «أريد».

nahhas-irab:89-89.t: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read «لا يُجرمنّكم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ. شِقاقِي is in the position of the nominative; أَنْ يُصِيبَكُمْ is in the position of the accusative. وَما قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِنْكُمْ بِبَعِيدٍ: al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. their dwellings are within your dwellings.

nahhas-irab:91-92.t: قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ ما نَفْقَهُ كَثِيراً مِمَّا تَقُولُ: one says faqiha yafqahu, when he understands, fiqhan and faqhan; al-Kisāʾī related «فقهانا» [Translator's note: so in the text]; and faquha fiqhan when he becomes a jurist (faqīh). وَإِنَّا لَنَراكَ فِينا ضَعِيفاً is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). وَلَوْلا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْناكَ: [«رهطك»] is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); likewise أَرَهْطِي, and the meaning is "is my clan greater in your hearts than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while He owns you?" وَاتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَراءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا: two objects.

nahhas-irab:93-93.t:
مَنْ is in the position of the accusative, like يَعْلَمُ الْمُفْسِدَ مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ [al-Baqara: 220]; وَمَنْ هُوَ كاذِبٌ is conjoined to it. Al-Farrāʾ permitted their position to be nominative by making them interrogative. What indicates the first view is that the second «من» is connected with a ṣila (relative clause), and it is impossible for it to be connected [as a relative] while interrogative. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that they brought «هو» in وَمَنْ هُوَ كاذِبٌ only because they do not say «من قائم» ("who [is] standing?"); they only say «من قام», «من يقوم» and «من القائم», so they added «هو» so that it would be a clause standing in place of faʿala and yafʿalu. Abū Jaʿfar said: what indicates the contrary of this is [the poet's] saying: [al-Khafīf] 220-
من رسول إلى الثّريّا بأنّي ... ضقت ذرعا بهجرها والكتاب
(Who [will be] a messenger to al-Thurayyā that I am at the end of my strength from her desertion and the letter?)

nahhas-irab:95-95.t: It is related that Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read كَما بَعُدَتْ ثَمُودُ with ḍamma on the ʿayn [Translator's note: the text prints بَعِدَتْ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: what is known in the language is that one says baʿida yabʿadu baʿadan and buʿdan when one perishes.

nahhas-irab:98-99.t: يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ: one says qadamahum yaqdumuhum qadman and qudūman when one goes ahead of them. وَبِئْسَ الْوِرْدُ: [«الورد»] is nominative by «بئس». الْمَوْرُودُ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or if you wish with an implied mubtadaʾ; likewise بئس الرِّفْدُ الْمَرْفُودُ. Al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayda related: rafadtuhu arfiduhu rafdan, i.e. I helped him and gave to him; and the noun for the gift is al-rifd.

nahhas-irab:100-100.t: ذلِكَ is nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that," or if you wish as a mubtadaʾ. Likewise مِنْها قائِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ, i.e. some of them are existing and built and some swallowed up [in the earth] and gone. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «حصيد» means «محصود» ("mown down"), and its plural is ḥaṣdā and ḥiṣād, like marḍā and mirāḍ. He said: and for rational beings ḥuṣadāʾ is permissible, like qabīl and qubalāʾ.

nahhas-irab:101-101.t: وَما ظَلَمْناهُمْ: the root meaning of ẓulm in the language is putting a thing in other than its place. وَلكِنْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ: Sībawayh related that one says «ظلم إياه». وَما زادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ: two objects; and it is figurative (majāz): since their worship of them had made them lose the reward of the Hereafter, it is said "they increased them only in loss."

nahhas-irab:102-102.t: وَكَذلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī read «وكذلك أخذ ربّك إذ أخذ القرى»; «إذ» is for the past, i.e. "when He seized the towns," while «إذا» is for the future, i.e. "whenever He seizes the towns." وَهِيَ ظالِمَةٌ, i.e. their people, like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:103-103.t: ذلِكَ يَوْمٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مَجْمُوعٌ is its naʿt (adjective). «الناس» is the noun of a verb whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), and for this reason it did not say «مجموعون». «الناس» may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «مجموع له» its khabar; and it did not say «مجموعون» because «له» stands in place of the agent.

nahhas-irab:105-105.t:
«يوم يأتي لا تكلم نفس إلا بإذنه» is the reading of the people of Medina, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, keeping the yāʾ in connected speech and dropping it in pause. It is related that Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them, read «يوم يأتي» keeping the yāʾ in pause and in connection. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read يَوْمَ يَأْتِ without yāʾ in pause and in connection. Abū Jaʿfar said: the right course in this is not to pause on it and to connect it with the yāʾ, because a group of grammarians said there is no justification for dropping the yāʾ, and a thing is not made jussive without a jussive-governing word. As for pausing without the yāʾ, there is al-Kisāʾī's view on it; he said: because a sound verb is paused on like a jussive one, so the yāʾ is dropped as the ḍamma is dropped. However, Abū ʿUbayd argued for dropping the yāʾ in pause and connection with two proofs. One is that he claimed he saw it in the Imām, which is called the Muṣḥaf of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, without yāʾ; the other proof is that he related that it is the dialect of Hudhayl, who say «ما أدر» ("I don't know"). Abū Jaʿfar said: as for his argument from the Muṣḥaf of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, it is something most scholars reject from him. Mālik ibn Anas, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I asked about the Muṣḥaf of ʿUthmān, may Allah be pleased with him, and was told it had gone. As for the argument from their saying «ما أدر», there is no proof in it, because the early grammarians related this word and mentioned its reason, and that no analogy is drawn from it. The reason for it according to Sībawayh — even though Sībawayh related «لا أدري» — is frequency of use, and the meaning of frequency of use is that it is a negation for everything one is ignorant of. Al-Farrāʾ recited regarding the dropping of the yāʾ: [al-Rajaz] 221-
كفّاك كفّ ما تليق درهما ... جودا وأخرى تعط بالسّيف الدّما
(Your two hands: one hand that out of generosity does not hold on to a dirham, and another that gives blood with the sword.)
لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ: the original is «تتكلّم»; one of the two tāʾs was dropped for lightness.

nahhas-irab:106-106.t: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); فَفِي النَّارِ is in the position of the khabar (predicate); likewise لَهُمْ فِيها زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: zafīr is from the chest and shahīq from the throat. Abū Isḥāq said: zafīr is from severe and ugly moaning, and shahīq is from very high-pitched moaning. He said: the philologists among the Basrans and the Kufans claimed that zafīr is like the beginning of the donkey's sound in braying, and shahīq like the end of the donkey's sound in braying.

nahhas-irab:107-107.t: خالِدِينَ فِيها is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ما دامَتِ السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "the lasting of the heavens and the earth," the implied construction being "the time of that." إِلَّا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ is in the position of the accusative, because it is an exception not from the first [category] (disjoined); we have already mentioned its meaning.

nahhas-irab:108-108.t:
Al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا with ḍamma on the sīn. Abū ʿAmr said: the proof that it is «سَعِدوا» is that the first is «شقوا» and He did not say «أُشقوا». Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān marvelling at al-Kisāʾī's reading سُعِدُوا despite his knowledge of Arabic, since this is a solecism that is not permissible, because one only says «سعد فلان» ("so-and-so was happy") and «أسعده الله» ("Allah made him happy"), so it is «أُسعد», like «أُمرض». Al-Kisāʾī argued only from their saying «مسعود», but he has no proof in it, because one says «مكان مسعود فيه» ("a place in which one is made happy"), then «فيه» is dropped and it is used as a name. He also argued from the Arabs' saying «فغر فاه» and «فغر فوه» ("he opened his mouth" / "his mouth opened"), and likewise «شحاه», «سار الدابة وسرته», «نزحت البئر ونزحتها» and «جبر العظم وجبرته»; but no analogy is drawn from this; only what the Arabs have uttered of it is uttered.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: if someone said to us, "How do you pronounce the transitive of «فغر فوه»?", we would only say «أفغرت فاه». What he said is good, and «فغر فاه» is not the transitive of that, but rather a separate dialectal form. عَطاءً is a noun standing for the maṣdar (verbal noun); غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ is its naʿt (adjective). One says «جذّه» and «حذّه» ("he cut it off"), as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 222-
تجذّ السّلوقيّ المضاعف نسجه ... ويوقدن بالصّفّاح نار الحباحب
(They cut through the double-woven Salūqī [mail], and kindle on the flint the sparks of al-ḥubāḥib.)

nahhas-irab:109-109.t: فَلا تَكُ is in the position of the jussive by the prohibition, and the nūn was dropped because of frequency of use. The best that has been said about its meaning is: say to everyone who doubts, فَلا تَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِمَّا يَعْبُدُ هؤُلاءِ, [for] Allah, Majestic and Mighty, did not command them to do it; they only worship them as their fathers used to do, in imitation of them.

nahhas-irab:110-110.t: وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ: the word is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, decreed to defer them until the Day of Resurrection, because of what He knew of the good in that. Were it not for that, judgement would have been passed between them by rewarding the believer and punishing the disbeliever. وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مُرِيبٍ: [«مريب»] is a naʿt (adjective) of «شكّ».

nahhas-irab:111-111.t:
وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَمَّا: there are eight readings of it, five of them agreeing with the written text (al-sawād). Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read with «إنّ» doubled and «لما» light. Nāfiʿ read with both of them light. Abū Jaʿfar [al-Qāriʾ], Shayba and Ḥamza — and it is the known reading of al-Aʿmash — read with both doubled. ʿĀṣim read with «إن» light and «لمّا» doubled. Al-Zuhrī read with «لمّا» doubled and with tanwīn. These are five readings. And it is reported from al-Aʿmash: وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا, with «إن» light, «كلّ» nominative and «لمّا» doubled.
Abū Ḥātim said: in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is «وإن كلّ إلّا ليوفّينّ ربّك أعمالهم», and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd «وإن كلّ إلّا ليوفّينّهم ربّك أعمالهم». Abū Jaʿfar said: the first reading is the clearest: «كلّا» is accusative by «إنّ», the lām is for emphasis, «ما» is connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant), and the khabar (predicate) is in «ليوفّينّهم»; the implied construction is "and indeed all, He will surely repay them in full." The reading of Nāfiʿ is on this same analysis, except that he lightened «إن» and made it operate as the heavy one operates. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh mentioned this, and for them it is like [the case where something] is dropped from a verb and it still operates, as [the poet] said: [al-Ṭawīl] 223-
كأن ظبية تعطو إلى ناضر السّلم
(As though [she were] a gazelle stretching up towards the fresh salam-tree.)
Al-Kisāʾī rejected that «إن» could be lightened and still operate, and said: I do not know on what basis he read «وإن كلّا». Al-Farrāʾ said: «كلّا» is accusative by His saying «لنوفّينّهم» [Translator's note: so in the text]. This is a great error; according to no one is «زيدا لأضربنّه» ("Zayd, I will surely beat him") permissible. The third reading, with both doubled, is a solecism according to most grammarians. It is related from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that this is not permissible: one does not say «إن زيدا إلا لأضربنّه» nor «[إن زيدا] لمّا لأضربنه». Al-Kisāʾī said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best about this reading; I know no justification for it. Abū Jaʿfar said: the grammarians have four views after this. Al-Farrāʾ said: the original is «وإنّ كلّا لَمِن ما», so three mīms came together and one of them was dropped. Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong, because he drops the nūn of «من» and only one letter remains. Abū ʿUthmān al-Māzinī said: the original is «وإنّ كلّا لَما» with «ما» light, then it was made heavy. Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong; the heavy is lightened, but the light is not made heavy. Abū ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām said: the original is وَإِنَّ كُلًّا لَمًّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ with tanwīn, from «لممته لمّا», i.e. I gathered it; then he formed faʿlā from it, as ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا تَتْرا [al-Muʾminūn: 44] was read without tanwīn and with tanwīn. Abū Isḥāq said: the view besides which nothing is permissible in my opinion is that «إن» is lightened from the heavy one and has the meaning of «ما» ("not"), like إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ [al-Ṭāriq: 4]; and likewise it is doubled according to its origin and has the meaning of «ما», while «لمّا» has the meaning of «إلّا» ("except"); al-Khalīl and Sībawayh related that. Abū Jaʿfar said: in the three readings that differ from the written text, «إن» has the meaning of «ما» and nothing else, and they are by way of exegesis (tafsīr), because it is not permissible to recite what differs from the written text except in this way.

nahhas-irab:113-113.t:
Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: وَلا تَرْكَنُوا is the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz. Al-Farrāʾ said: the dialect of Tamīm and Qays is rakana yarkunu. It is related from Qatāda that he read وَلا تَرْكُنُوا with ḍamma on the kāf [Translator's note: the text prints تَرْكَنُوا in both places]. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read فَتِمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ [Translator's note: the text prints فَتَمَسَّكُمُ; the variant with kasra on the tāʾ is what is discussed]. Abū ʿUbayd rejected this, saying: because there is no guttural letter in it. Abū Jaʿfar said: there is no sense in his saying "there is no guttural letter in it," because guttural letters do not attract kasra. This dialect was mentioned by al-Khalīl and Sībawayh from other than the people of the Ḥijāz: when the verb is on the pattern faʿila, they give kasra to the first [letter] of its imperfect to indicate the kasra in its past; the second [letter] ought to have had kasra to agree with the past, but that was not possible because the second is necessarily quiescent, so they gave kasra to the first, saying «يِحذر». It is well known among Banū Fazāra and Hudhayl, as [the poet] said:
[al-Kāmil] 224-
وإخال إنّي لاحق مستتبع
(And I think that I am overtaken, being pursued.)
Likewise, when there is a conjunctive alif with kasra in its past, they give kasra to the first [letter] of the imperfect, such as «نِستعين». Sībawayh said: and likewise whatever ought to have had a conjunctive alif, such as tafaʿʿala and tafāʿala.

nahhas-irab:114-114.t: وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهارِ: [«طرفي»] is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); the nūn was dropped because of annexation, and the yāʾ was given kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; it was not dropped because what precedes it has fatḥa. (وزلفا) is conjoined (maʿṭūf). Abū Jaʿfar [al-Qāriʾ] read وَزُلُفاً with ḍamma on the zāy and the lām, and it is the plural of zalīf, because zalīf is attested; it may also be a singular. Ibn Muḥayṣin read وَزُلْفاً مِنَ اللَّيْلِ with ḍamma on the zāy, sukūn on the lām and tanwīn; it is a form with sukūn from «زُلُف», not from «زُلَف», since the fatḥa is light [Translator's note: the text reads «لأزلف», as written; the Quranic forms in this entry are printed as زُلَفاً, without the variants' vowelling]. إِنَّ الْحَسَناتِ: it has been said that by this the prayers are meant. It is undisputed that repentance removes evil deeds, and that avoiding the major sins removes the minor evil deeds.

nahhas-irab:116-116.t: فَلَوْلا has the meaning of «هلّا» ("why not"); the Arabs use this for expressing wonder at a thing, i.e. "why then was there not, among the generations before you, a people…" يَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْفَسادِ فِي الْأَرْضِ, because of the minds Allah, Majestic and Mighty, gave them and the signs He showed them. إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّنْ أَنْجَيْنا مِنْهُمْ is an exception not from the first [category] (disjoined). وَاتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ما أُتْرِفُوا فِيهِ, i.e. of preoccupation with wealth and pleasures.

nahhas-irab:118-118.t: وَلا يَزالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ: [«مختلفين»] is the khabar (predicate) of «يزال».

nahhas-irab:119-119.t: (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ): an istithnāʾ (exception). (وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ): the meaning of (تمّت) is "was established", that is, as He had foretold it.

nahhas-irab:120-120.t: (وَكُلًّا) is accusative (manṣūb) by (نقصّ). (ما نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ), that is, in patience in conveying the Message; and (ما) is a badal (substitute) for (كلّ). Al-Akhfash said: «وكلّا» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the ḥāl being placed first, just as you say: كلّا ضربت القوم ("all of them, I struck the people"). (وَمَوْعِظَةٌ), that is, that by which one takes admonition, from the destruction of the nations. (وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ), that is, they call to mind what befell those who perished, and so they guard themselves. «[Translator's note: the source prints «نصب بنقص» and «فيتوفّون»; the former is evidently «نقصّ» (We relate) and the latter is rendered here as if «فيتوقّون» (they guard themselves), which the context suggests.]»

nahhas-irab:123-123.t: Al-Akhfash said: «وما ربك بغافل عما يعملون» ("…of what they do"), when the Prophet ﷺ is not addressed together with them. He said: and some read (تَعْمَلُونَ) ("you do"), because He addressed the Prophet ﷺ together with them, or [because] He said, "Say to them: (وَما رَبُّكَ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ)."
